brief: Mapped horseshoe palace and distinct Kaiser, Markgraf, Bishop, Michael and Watch towers, two separately shaped chapels, bastion ring and multilevel open entrance ramps with gate tunnels.

nativeAxes.origin: Signed enclosure anchor; Y0 decoded 835.9281 m numeric terrain working datum.

sourceFacts.identity: Exact Q156457 on OSM way/93612350; enclosure is not a building footprint
sourceFacts.referenceState: Normal exterior architecture from the official illustrated plan, Stüler 1854 design elevations and a 2005 courtyard photograph; temporary 2026 restoration scaffolding is excluded.

reconstruction.basis: Individual OSM parts constrain the horizontal plan. Official visitor illustration distinguishes bastions and ramp levels. Historical architect elevations and courtyard photography guide unique towers, roofs and facade detail.
reconstruction.verticalDatum: Fresh exact-Q156457 enclosure way 93612350 v51 and 43 mapped parts use native +X ESE at 104.564815 degrees, +Z SSW at 194.564815 degrees, heading -0.254203978258. Several shared entrance nodes changed since the original source: up to 12.203 m nearest-vertex displacement is recorded as a map-version difference. The independent derivative uses fresh geometry; original evidence and recipe remain reproducible. Eagle and upper gate passage centers/bearings follow the mapped covered roads. Retained coarse numeric terrain has a 4225-value 4 m native grid and decoded anchor working datum 835.9281 m. One rigid -10.4563 m shift meets mapped approach grade +0.08 m; court is 19.5437 m above anchor. The 30 m relative entry-to-court rise remains a reconstruction supported by independent 825/855 map tags, not a connected vertical survey. Only the lowest owned entrance roads and Eagle gate use a 434.096-square-meter ground cut; its enclosed island retains sampled grade. Upper court and mountain remain uncut. Mapped structural skirts extend four meters below retained terrain.
reconstruction.state: 19th-century neo-Gothic palace, with surviving older St Michael chapel and open fortified entrance.

Coarse terrain does not resolve the sharp summit, bastion feet or covered spiral entrance; exact vertical datum, native resolution and vintage remain unverified.

One rigid shift puts the fresh mapped approach start 0.08 m above decoded grade. The existing 30 m relative court height is retained as an explicit reconstruction; independent map elevation tags 825 and 855 are not a connected survey.
Mapped structural skirts extend below sampled terrain. A narrow connected lowest-road and Eagle-gate ground cut clears only owned civil surfaces; upper court and mountain remain host terrain.

Accepted exterior scope includes the horseshoe palace, independent tower forms, two chapels, court, bastion enclosure and multilevel spiral entrance. The forested mountain, water tower, parking buildings, ivy, statuary, museum rooms and inaccessible casemates are separate scope.

Normal architecture follows the official illustrated plan, historic design elevations and courtyard photograph; temporary restoration scaffolding is omitted. These are not measured current elevations. Fine facade/window counts, gate body envelopes and vault shapes remain approximate.

Six reusable graphs provide granite, sandstone, limestone, timber, painted metal and slate. Carved trim shares sandstone with distinct tint; slate courses use the shared texture rather than copied roof geometry. Opaque PBR glass and garden tint have no images. Skyline bakes common linear means; physical phone/laptop timings remain unmeasured.
